$description: IBCS design tokens: colours, patterns, geometry, typography, number/date formats and abbreviations, for reports that follow the IBCS® Standards. Format: W3C Design Tokens (DTCG) with $value/$type; provenance in $extensions.ibcs.src (STD = stated by IBCS/ISO 24896, REC = IBCS recommendation, FIG = read/measured from an IBCS figure, OURS = our default where IBCS is silent, ORG = set by a corporate override). IBCS prescribes no hex codes. Values follow IBCS Standards v2.0 (2026-07-16); refs such as 'UN 4.1' cite its rule numbers. This file is data under the MIT License. IBCS® is a registered trademark of IBCS Institute; not affiliated with or certified by IBCS Institute. See the ibcs-notation skill, references/tokens-in-practice.md, for structure, overrides and consumption.

scenario.$description: Scenario notation lives in the fill pattern (solid dark / solid light / outlined / hatched), never in hue (UN 3.2).

ac.$description: Actual (AC): solid dark fill; also line colour, filled square markers, thick dark table-header rule.

ibcs.ref: UN 3.2, p. 43-44; Fig. UN 4.1-3 dark gray

py.$description: Previous year / previous period (PY): solid light fill, ONLY in scenario comparisons (not in plain time series).

fill.$description: Plan (PL): outlined = empty fill ('fill up when materializing'); fill = page background.

ibcs.ref: UN 3.2, p. 45 (outlined/empty rule STD, hex FIG)

stroke.$description: Plan outline in the AC colour.

stripe.$description: Forecast (FC): hatched; dark stripes = colour of measured data. Geometry in pattern.fcHatch.

stroke.$description: Dark outline around hatched FC shapes.

stackGrays.$description: Segment shades for stacked columns/bars/areas and multi-series, darkest at the axis. The lowest segment carries the scenario notation; upper segments get different gray shades (+ outline for PL, hatch for FC). Note: array value (not a plain DTCG colour); a merge replaces it wholesale.

variance.$description: Three impact states (UN 4.1, pp. 52-54): desirable = bright green, undesirable = dark red, neutral/ambiguous = blue. The HUES are fixed by IBCS; only the exact codes are an organisational choice. Colour is chosen by business impact (measure polarity); geometry always follows the arithmetic sign (an increase goes up/right even for a cost line). Not traffic lights (EX 2.5). Also used for difference markers, trend arrows, outlier triangles.

goodText.$description: Text colour for a variance NUMBER tinted by impact (decision: a variance number may be tinted only with a colour that meets 4.5:1 text contrast on color.background.page, WCAG 1.4.3; otherwise it stays color.text.primary). Darker green of the same hue family as color.variance.good: 5.0:1 on white (the bright graphic green is 2.4:1 and must not be used for text). Bars, pins and markers keep color.variance.good.

badText.$description: Text colour for a variance NUMBER tinted by impact (decision: a variance number may be tinted only with a colour that meets 4.5:1 text contrast on color.background.page, WCAG 1.4.3; otherwise it stays color.text.primary). Dark red, 5.7:1 on white (the graphic red #FF0000 is 4.0:1). Stays darker than goodText, as for the graphic colours.

neutralText.$description: Text colour for a variance NUMBER tinted by impact (decision: a variance number may be tinted only with a colour that meets 4.5:1 text contrast on color.background.page, WCAG 1.4.3; otherwise it stays color.text.primary). The neutral blue already meets 4.5:1 on white (4.9:1); override it together with color.variance.neutral if that changes.

cvd.$description: Colour-vision-deficiency variant: green -> blue-green; keep desirable bright, undesirable dark.

goodText.$description: Text variant of the CVD blue-green (5.6:1 on white; the graphic #008E96 is 4.0:1).

bw.$description: No-colour (black & white) variant: good light gray, neutral medium gray, bad dark gray.

ibcs.ref: UN 4.1, Fig. UN 4.1-3 (shade rule STD, hex FIG)
UN 4.1, Fig. UN 4.1-3 (shade rule STD, hex FIG)
UN 4.1, Fig. UN 4.1-3 (shade rule STD, hex FIG)

highlight.$description: Highlighting ellipse around the value the key message refers to; single highlighted element (e.g. one bar).

ibcs.note: Legend figure uses #42BCEF; tone not fixed by IBCS.

annotationRef.$description: Numbered annotation reference circles (used in pairs).

referenceArrowhead.$description: Black arrowhead for index (100%) and benchmark references.

ibcs.ref: UN 4.2, UN 4.3, UN 5.1 (black arrowhead rule STD, hex FIG)

scaleBandFill.$description: Scale band area: light colour (e.g. light blue) from category axis to the common value.

scaleBandLine.$description: Scale band line and its value label.

adjustment.$description: Light-blue segment for inflation/currency effects (AC* analyses).

assistingLine.$description: Thin assisting lines/areas: connectors, separators, difference-marker projections, AC/FC separator ticks.

assistingArea.$description: Light area to group or highlight text/chart parts (e.g. reference panel in small multiples).

secondary.$description: Footnotes, sources, secondary series labels. 7.0:1 on white.

onAc.$description: Labels on an AC-filled mark, regardless of theme mode.

onDark.$description: Deprecated alias of color.text.onAc; use onAc for labels on AC-filled marks.

page.$description: Page and visual background: white, no fills, no bands, no wallpaper.

category.$description: Thin dark category axis (baseline). Variance-chart axes use stroke.varianceAxis.* instead.

pyReference.$description: Axis of variance charts whose subtrahend is PY: solid light, thick.

plReference.$description: Axis of variance charts whose subtrahend is PL/BU: two parallel thin dark lines.

grid.$description: Grid lines: OFF by default; allowed only in dense charts, small multiples, scatter/bubble.

rule.$description: Header underline (non-scenario columns), rule above totals/result rows.

ruleLight.$description: Thin horizontal separators between rows. No vertical rules.

totalFill.$description: Optional light-gray background of totals/result rows/columns.

fcHatch.$description: Forecast hatch. Stripes rising bottom-left to top-right ('////'), dark stripe = color.scenario.fc.stripe on color.scenario.fc.ground, shape outlined with color.scenario.fc.stroke. Also used for hatched variance fills (FC minuend) with the impact colour as stripe colour.

stripeShare.$description: Dark share of one period (stripe width = periodPx × stripeShare).

svgTemplate.$value: <pattern id="ibcs-fc-hatch" patternUnits="userSpaceOnUse" width="4" height="4" patternTransform="rotate(45)"><rect width="4" height="4" fill="#FFFFFF"/><rect width="1.8" height="4" fill="#404040"/></pattern>
svgTemplate.$description: Reference SVG pattern built from the tokens above (regenerate if overridden). Vega-Lite has no pattern fill: use SVG/Deneb-Vega or a stripe layer.

geometry.$description: Ratios are relative to the category width (band) unless stated otherwise.

absolute.$description: Columns/bars of absolute measures: width = 2/3 of category width (gap 1/3). Vega-Lite paddingInner 0.333.

relative.$description: Columns/bars of relative measures (%, ratios, shares): 1/3 of category width. Vega-Lite paddingInner 0.667.

variance.$description: Absolute variance columns/bars: SAME width (and same scale) as their base columns/bars.

thicknessRatio.$description: Pin body thickness relative to the base bar thickness. Clamp the result to geometry.pin.stemPx (px).

headRatio.$description: Pin head edge relative to the base bar thickness (square is the illustrated default, not a mandate). Head fill = minuend scenario (AC solid, FC hatched). Clamp the result to geometry.pin.headPx (px).

stemPx.$description: Pin stem thickness clamp in px, applied after the ratio × bar thickness. Use the same clamp in every renderer (SVG/React, Deneb/Vega, SVG-in-DAX).

headPx.$description: Pin head edge clamp in px, applied after the ratio × bar thickness. Use the same clamp in every renderer (SVG/React, Deneb/Vega, SVG-in-DAX).

column.$description: Overlapped grouping: reference column (PY/PL) behind AC/FC, shifted LEFT by this share of its width.

bar.$description: Overlapped grouping: reference bar behind, shifted UP by this share of its thickness.

triangleSizeRatio.$description: Scenario triangle height relative to the column width / bar thickness. Columns: right-pointing, left of column. Bars: down-pointing, above bar. Clamp the result to geometry.triangleSizePx (px).

triangleSizePx.$description: Scenario triangle size (height) clamp in px, applied after geometry.triangleSizeRatio × column width / bar thickness. Use the same clamp in every renderer (SVG/React, Deneb/Vega, SVG-in-DAX).

remainderGapRatio.$description: Extra gap before a remainder bar/row ('Other', 'Rest of …'), in category heights.

categoryWidthByPeriod.$description: Relative category width per period type (longer period -> wider); fixed per period type for at least a page/screen.

categoryStepPx.$description: Screen defaults for band step per period type (px).

structureRow.$description: Band step for structure categories in bar charts / table rows.

stroke.$description: Line widths. *Pt values for print/Power BI, *Px for screens.

absolutePt.$description: Thick line for absolute measures (≈0.6-0.7 mm).

relativeRatio.$description: Thin line for relative measures = 50% of thick.

markerToLineRatio.$description: Point-marker edge relative to line width. Scenario lives in the MARKERS on a continuous line: AC filled, PL hollow/outlined, FC hatched (never dashed lines). Line thickness encodes absolute vs relative, not scenario.

outlinePx.$description: Outline width for PL/BU shapes (print ≈0.35-0.5 mm).

pyWidthMm.$description: Solid light axis for variances vs PY.

plLineMm.$description: Each of the two parallel lines for variances vs PL/BU.

plGapMm.$description: Centre-to-centre distance of the two PL axis lines.

plGapPx.$description: Centre-to-centre (i.e. 2 px white between two 1 px lines).

scenarioPx.$description: Header underline encoding the scenario: AC thick dark, PY thick light, FC thick hatched; PL/BU = double thin dark (two 1 px lines, 1 px gap).

plainPx.$description: Thin single line under structure/measure/time/variance headers.

powerbi.$description: Plain, widely available sans-serif. Semibold only for semantic emphasis.

emphasis.$description: ONLY for measure names in title line 2, totals/results rows and columns, defined subtotals. Italic only for semantically defined rows ('percent of').

size.$description: Screen defaults. pt for Power BI, px for web. IBCS gives no sizes: 'as small as possible, still legible' (CO 1). Phone layouts +1 pt / +2 px; web never below 12 px.

title.$description: All three title lines same size; line 2 measure in emphasis weight.

label.$description: Data labels, category labels, integrated legends, table cells.

ofWhich.$description: 'Of which' / 'percent of' rows and columns: smaller (web keeps 12 px minimum, use secondary colour instead).

orientation.$description: Legends, category labels and data labels are never rotated.

thousands.$description: Narrow no-break space U+202F (ISO 80000-1 narrow space).

range.$description: Time spans: two full stops, no blanks (Jan..Mar).

negative.$description: Hyphen-minus for exports/CSV safety; U+2212 is an acceptable override.

plus.$description: Plus sign ONLY on variances (ΔPY, ΔPL, ΔPY%, pp); never on plain values.

notApplicable.$description: Shown instead of a relative variance when the reference is ≤ 0 or blank (our derivation of UN 4.1 p. 54). Examples: PL 100 / AC -20 → -120 % (shown); PL -30 / AC -10 → N/A. Always computed with the SIGNED reference, never ABS().

ibcs.ref: UN 4.1 p. 53-54 (N/A concept STD, ≤ 0 rule OURS)

scaling.$description: Prefixes: monetary lower-case single letter attached to the ISO 4217 code (kEUR); non-monetary SI (k, M, G). The unit lives in title line 2 / subtitle, not on every value.

rule.$value: Pick one prefix per visual (per scale group) so the largest |value| shows ≤ maxDigits.chart integer digits; 1 decimal if the largest |value| < 100, else 0 decimals.

format.$description: Format patterns per value kind. d3 = d3-format/Vega-Lite (replace ',' group separator with number.separator.thousands after formatting); excel = Power BI/DAX/Excel format string (thousands separator comes from the culture).

relativeVariance1.$description: Relative variance with one decimal (+5.8%), for specs whose display setting asks for it (decimals fixed per scale group). Default stays relativeVariance (whole percent).

plainRatio.$description: Plain ratio that is not a percentage (book-to-bill, coverage, current ratio): 1.01, no % sign, unit 'ratio' in the title. Its variance uses the same decimals with a sign (+0.03).

currency.$description: EUR, USD, CHF, GBP — no €/$/£ symbols when currencies mix.

month.$description: Jan, Feb … when the year is in the title (SI 4.3).

notation.$description: Analysis prefixes/suffixes applied to a period label x.

abbreviation.$description: Codes used in labels, headers and title line 3. Long forms for glossary/tooltips.

PP.$description: Same notation as PY. Code is OURS.

ΔPY%.$value: (AC − PY) / PY × 100, signed reference; N/A if reference ≤ 0 or blank

ΔPL%.$value: (AC − PL) / PL × 100, signed reference; N/A if reference ≤ 0 or blank

ΔBU%.$value: (AC − BU) / BU × 100, signed reference; N/A if reference ≤ 0 or blank

AC-PL.$value: explicit form when AC/FC is ambiguous; likewise FC-PL, AC-PY, FC-PY, (AC-PL)% …

scenarioOrder.$description: Default left→right / top→bottom order for scenario columns of the SAME period (by creation time: PL, FC, AC; PY first as an earlier period). Different periods: ascending time.

varianceOrder.$description: Variance column order in tables (EX 1.2-23). Pairs separated by layout.table.groupGapPx.

polarity.$description: Per-measure attribute that selects the impact COLOUR only (never the geometry; never plot Δ × polarity): polarity 0 → neutral (blue); otherwise Δ = 0 → no bar and default text colour (never bad), good if Δ × polarity > 0, bad if < 0.

layout.$description: Page grid defaults. IBCS gives no numbers (CO 1-2: narrow margins, smallest legible). Standardise per page type in the notation manual.

marginPx.$description: Outer margin; also the web side gutter at phone width.

columnGapPx.$description: Narrow gap B1 between columns of the same type.

groupGapPx.$description: Wide gap B2 between column groups and after the row-header column.

maxPanels.$description: ≈25 panels max; beyond that add an 'Others' panel.
